content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Cor Iesu amóre nostri vulnerátum * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Sacred Heart of Jesus, which was wounded for love of us, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Cor Iesu amóre nostri vulnerátum * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Sacred Heart of Jesus, which was wounded for love of us, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.english: O Christ, the world's Creator bright,

content.latin: Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
content.english: Who didst mankind from sin redeem,

content.latin: Lumen Patris de lúmine,
content.english: Light from the Father's glorious light,

content.latin: Deúsque verus de Deo.
content.english: True God of God, in bliss supreme.

content.latin: Amor coégit te tuus
content.english: Thy love compelled thee to assume

content.english: Reversing the old Adam's doom;

content.latin: Quod vetus ille abstúlerat.
content.english: Our ransom the new Adam gave.

content.latin: Ille amor, almus ártifex
content.english: That love which gloriously framed all

content.latin: Terræ marísque, et síderum,
content.english: The earth, the stars, and wondrous sea

content.latin: Erráta patrum míserans,
content.english: Took pity on our parents' fall,

content.latin: Et nostra rumpens víncula.
content.english: Broke all our bonds and set us free.

content.latin: Non Corde discédat tuo
content.english: O Saviour, let thy potent love

content.latin: Vis illa amóris íncliti:
content.english: Flow ever from thy bounteous heart;

content.latin: Hoc fonte gentes háuriant
content.english: To nations that pure fount above

content.english: The grace of pardon will impart.

content.latin: Percússum ad hoc est láncea,
content.english: His heart for this was opened wide,

content.latin: Passúmque ad hoc est vúlnera:
content.english: And wounded by the soldier's spear,

content.latin: Ut nos laváret sórdibus,
content.english: That freely from his sacred side

content.latin: Unda fluénte, et sánguine.
content.english: Might flow the streams our souls to clear.

content.latin: Iesu, tibi sit glória,
content.english: Glory to Father and to Son,

content.latin: Qui Corde fundis grátiam,

content.latin: Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
content.english: To whom all power, when time is done,

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.

content.latin: Psalmus 32 [1]
content.english: Psalm 32 [1]

content.latin: 32:1 Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
content.english: 32:1 Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.

content.latin: 32:2 Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
content.english: 32:2 Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.

content.latin: 32:3 Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
content.english: 32:3 Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.

content.latin: 32:4 Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.
content.english: 32:4 For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.

content.latin: 32:5 Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
content.english: 32:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

content.latin: 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.
content.english: 32:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:

content.latin: 32:7 Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
content.english: 32:7 Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.

content.latin: 32:8 Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
content.english: 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.

content.latin: 32:9 Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 32:9 For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.

content.latin: 32:10 Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
content.english: 32:10 The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.

content.latin: 32:11 Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 32:11 But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

content.latin: 32:12 Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
content.english: 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

content.latin: 32:13 De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
content.english: 32:13 The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.

content.latin: 32:14 De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
content.english: 32:14 From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.

content.latin: 32:15 Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
content.english: 32:15 He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.

content.latin: 32:16 Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
content.english: 32:16 The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.

content.latin: 32:17 Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
content.english: 32:17 Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.

content.latin: 32:18 Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:
content.english: 32:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.

content.latin: 32:19 Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
content.english: 32:19 To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.

content.latin: 32:20 Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.
content.english: 32:20 Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.

content.latin: 32:21 Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.
content.english: 32:21 For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.

content.latin: 32:22 Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: 32:22 Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.

content.english: Psalm 35 [2]

content.latin: 35:2 Dixit iniústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eius.
content.english: 35:2 The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.

content.latin: 35:3 Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu eius: * ut inveniátur iníquitas eius ad ódium.
content.english: 35:3 For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.

content.latin: 35:4 Verba oris eius iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
content.english: 35:4 The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.

content.latin: 35:5 Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
content.english: 35:5 He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.

content.latin: 35:6 Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
content.english: 35:6 O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.

content.latin: 35:7 Iustítia tua sicut montes Dei: * iudícia tua abýssus multa.
content.english: 35:7 Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.

content.latin: 35:7 Hómines, et iuménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
content.english: 35:7 Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!

content.latin: 35:8 Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
content.english: 35:8 But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.

content.latin: 35:9 Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
content.english: 35:9 They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.

content.latin: 35:10 Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
content.english: 35:10 For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.

content.latin: 35:11 Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et iustítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 35:11 Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.

content.latin: 35:12 Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
content.english: 35:12 Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.

content.latin: 35:13 Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
content.english: 35:13 There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.

content.latin: Psalmus 40 [3]
content.english: Psalm 40 [3]

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

content.english: ℣. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me.

content.english: ℟. For I am meek and lowly in Heart.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: Lesson from the book of Jeremias

content.latin: 5 Hæc dicit Dóminus, Deus Israël: Cognóscam transmigratiónem Iuda, quam emísi de loco isto in terram Chaldæórum, in bonum.
content.english: 5 Thus saith the Lord the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so will I regard the captives of Juda, whom I have sent forth out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans, for their good.

content.latin: 6 Et ponam óculos meos super eos ad placándum, et redúcam eos in terram hanc; et ædificábo eos, et non déstruam; et plantábo eos et non evéllam.
content.english: 6 And I will set my eyes upon them to be pacified, and I will bring them again into this land: and I will build them up, and not pull them down: and I will plant them, and not pluck them up.

content.latin: 7 Et dabo eis cor ut sciant me, quia ego sum Dóminus; et erunt mihi in pópulum, et ego ero eis in Deum, quia reverténtur ad me in toto corde suo.
content.english: 7 And I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: because they shall return to me with their whole heart.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Fériam eis pactum sempitérnum et non désinam eis benefácere et timórem meum dabo in corde eórum
content.english: ℟. I will make an everlasting Covenant with them, and I will not cease from doing them good, and I will put my fear in their hearts,

content.english: 18 Thus saith the Lord: Behold I will bring back the captivity of the pavilions of Jacob, and will have pity on his houses, and the city shall be built in her high place, and the temple shall be founded according to the order thereof.

content.latin: 19 Et egrediétur de eis laus, voxque ludéntium.
content.english: 19 And out of them shall come forth praise, and the voice of them that play:

content.latin: 21 Et erit dux eius ex eo, et princeps de médio eius producétur; et, applicábo eum et accédet ad me. Quis enim iste est qui ápplicet cor suum ut appropínquet mihi? ait Dóminus.
content.english: 21 And their leader shall be of themselves: and their prince shall come forth from the midst of them: and I will bring him near, and he shall come to me: for who is this that setteth his heart to approach to me, saith the Lord?

content.latin: 22 Et éritis mihi in pópulum, et ego ero vobis in Deum.

content.latin: 23 Ecce turbo Dómini, furor egrédiens, procélla ruens; in cápite impiórum conquiéscet.
content.english: 23 Behold the whirlwind of the Lord, his fury going forth, a violent storm, it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.

content.latin: 24 Non avértet iram indignatiónis Dóminus, donec fáciat et cómpleat cogitatiónem Cordis sui: in novíssimo diérum intellegétis ea.
content.english: 24 The Lord will not turn away the wrath of his indignation, till he have executed and performed the thought of his heart: in the latter days you shall understand these things.

content.latin: 1 In témpore illo, dicit Dóminus, ero Deus univérsis cognatiónibus Israël, et ipsi erunt mihi in pópulum.

content.latin: 2 Hæc dicit Dóminus: Invénit grátiam in desérto pópulus qui remánserat a gládio; vadet ad réquiem suam Israël.
content.english: 2 Thus saith the Lord: The people that were left and escaped from the sword, found grace in the desert: Israel shall go to his rest.

content.latin: 3 Longe Dóminus appáruit mihi. Et in caritáte perpétua diléxi te: ídeo attráxi te, míserans.
content.english: 3 The Lord hath appeared from afar to me. Yea I have loved thee with an everlasting love, therefore have I drawn thee, taking pity on thee.

content.latin: 31 Ecce dies vénient, dicit Dóminus: et fériam dómui Israël et dómui Iuda fœdus novum:
content.english: 31 Behold the days shall come, saith the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda:

content.latin: 32 Non secúndum pactum, quod pépigi cum pátribus eórum in die, qua apprehéndi manum eórum, ut edúcerem eos de Terra Ægýpti: pactum quod írritum fecérunt, et ego dominátus sum eórum, dicit Dóminus.
content.english: 32 Not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt: the covenant which they made void, and I had dominion over them, saith the Lord.

content.latin: 33 Sed hoc erit pactum, quod fériam cum domo Israël: post dies illos dicit Dóminus: Dabo legem meam in viscéribus eórum, et in corde eórum scribam eam: et ero eis in Deum, et ipsi erunt mihi in pópulum.
content.english: 33 But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel, after those days, saith the Lord: I will give my law in their bowels, and I will write it in their heart: and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

content.latin: Inter mira sacræ doctrínæ pietatísque increménta, quibus divínæ Sapiéntiæ consília clárius in dies Ecclésiæ manifestántur, vix áliud magis conspícuum est quam triumphális progréssio cultus sacratíssimi Cordis Iesu. Sǽpius quidem, priórum decúrsu témporum, Patres, Doctóres, Sancti, Redemptóris nostri amórem celebrárunt: vulnus in látere Christi apértum ómnium gratiárum arcánum dixérunt fontem. At inde a médio ævo, cum tenerióre quadam erga sanctíssimam Salvatóris Humanitátem religióne fidéles áffici cœpti sunt, ánimæ contemplatívæ per plagam illam ad ipsum Cor, amóre hóminum vulnerátum, penetráre fere solébant. Atque ex eo témpore hæc contemplátio sanctíssimis quibúsque ita familiáris evásit, ut neque régio neque ordo religiósus sit, in quibus non insígnia, hac ætáte, eius reperiántur testimónia. Próximis demum sǽculis, eóque potíssimum témpore quo hærétici, sub falsæ pietátis título, a sanctíssima Eucharístia Christiános detérrere conabántur, cultus sacratíssimo Cordi públice exhibéri cœptus est, ópera imprímis sancti Ioánnis Eudes, qui auctor litúrgici cultus sacrórum Córdium Iesu et Maríæ haud immérito nuncupátur.
content.english: Among the wonderful developments of sacred teaching and piety, by which the plans of the divine Wisdom are daily made clear to the Church, hardly any is more manifest than the triumphant progress made by the devotion of the most Sacred Heart of Jesus. Very often indeed, during the course of past ages, Fathers, Doctors, and Saints have celebrated our Redeemer's love: and they have said, that the wound opened in the side of Christ was the hidden fountain of all graces. Moreover, from the Middle Ages onward, when the faithful began to show a more tender piety towards the most sacred Humanity of the Saviour, contemplative souls became accustomed to penetrate through that wound almost to the very Heart itself, wounded for the love of men. And from that time, this form of contemplation became so familiar to all persons of saintly life, that there was no country or religious order in which, during this period, witnesses to it were not to be found. Finally, during recent centuries, and most especially at that period when heretics, in the name of a false piety, strove to discourage Christians from receiving the most Holy Eucharist, the veneration of the most Sacred Heart began to be openly practised, principally through the exertions of St. John Eudes, who is by no means unworthily called the founder of the liturgical worship of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

content.latin: Verum, ad cultum sacratíssimi Cordis Iesu plene perfectéque constituéndum, eundémque per totum orbem propagándum, Deus ipse sibi instruméntum elégit humíllimam ex órdine Visitatiónis vírginem, sanctam Margarítam Maríam Alacóque, cui, a prima quidem ætáte iam in Eucharístiæ Sacraméntum amóre flagránti, Christus Dóminus sæpenúmero appárens, divíni Cordis sui et divítias et optáta significáre dignátus est. Quarum apparitiónum celebérrima illa est, qua ei ante Eucharístiam oránti Iesus conspiciéndum se dedit, sacratíssimum Cor osténdit et conquéstus quod, pro imménsa sua caritáte, nihil nisi ingratórum hóminum contumélias recíperet, ipsi præcépit ut novum festum, féria sexta post Octávam Córporis Christi, instituéndum curáret, quo Cor suum honóre débito colerétur, atque iniúriæ sibi in Sacraménto amóris a peccatóribus illátæ dignis expiaréntur obséquiis. Quot autem quantásque Dei fámula in Christi mandátis exsequéndis expérta sit difficultátes, nemo est qui ignóret; sed ab ipso Dómino confirmáta, atque a religiósis ánimæ suæ moderatóribus, qui incredíbili quodam ardóre ad hunc cultum promovéndum laborárunt, strénue adiúta, múnere sibi cǽlitus commísso fidéliter fungi ad mortem usque non déstitit.
content.english: But in order to establish fully and entirely the worship of the most Sacred Heart of Jesus, and to spread the same throughout the whole world, God himself chose as his instrument a most humble virgin from the order of the Visitation, St. Margaret Mary Alacoque, who even in her earliest years already had a burning love for the Sacrament of the Eucharist, and to whom Christ the Lord had very many times appeared, and was pleased to make known the riches and the desires of his divine Heart. The most famous of these apparitions was that in which Jesus revealed himself to her in prayer before the blessed Sacrament, shewed her his most Sacred Heart, and, complaining that in return for his unbounded love, he met with nothing but outrages and ingratitude from mankind, he ordered her to concern herself with the establishment of a new feast, on the Friday after the Octave of Corpus Christi, on which his Heart should be venerated with due honour, and that the insults offered him by sinners in the Sacrament of love should be expiated by worthy satisfaction. But there is no one who knoweth not how many and how great were the obstacles which the handmaid of God experienced, in carrying out the commands of Christ; but, endowed with strength by the Lord himself, and actively aided by her pious spiritual directors, who exerted themselves with an almost unbelievable zeal, up to the time of her death she never ceased faithfully to carry out the duty entrusted to her by heaven.

content.latin: Anno tandem millésimo septingentésimo sexagésimo quinto, Clemens décimus tértius Póntifex Máximus offícium et missam in honórem sacratíssimi Cordis Iesu approbávit; Pius vero nonus festum ad univérsam Ecclésiam exténdit. Exínde, cultus sacratíssimi Cordis, quasi flumen exúndans, prolútis impediméntis ómnibus, per totum se orbem effúdit, et, novo illucescénte sǽculo, iubilǽo indícto, Leo décimus tértius humánum genus univérsum sacratíssimo Cordi devótum vóluit. Quæ consecrátio, in ómnibus quidem cathólici orbis ecclésiis, solémni ritu perácta, ingens áttulit devotiónis huius increméntum, et ad eam non solum pópulos, verum étiam singuláres famílias addúxit, quæ Divíno Cordi innumerábiles se dévovent, regióque eius império subíciunt. Dénique, Pius undécimus Póntifex Máximus, quo plénius festi solémnitas pópuli christiáni devotióni tam late paténti respondéret, sacratíssimi Cordis Iesu festum ad ritum dúplicem primæ classis cum octáva evéxit; ac prætérea, ut violáta iura Christi summi Regis ac Dómini amantíssimi resarciréntur, populorúmque peccáta defleréntur, eódem festo die piaculárem precatiónem in ómnibus christiáni orbis templis quotánnis recitándam mandávit.
content.english: At length, in the year 1765, the Supreme Pontiff Clement XIII approved the Mass and Office in honour of the most Sacred Heart of Jesus; and Pius IX extended the feast to the universal Church. From then on the worship of the most Sacred Heart, like an overflowing river, washing away all obstacles, hath poured itself forth over all the earth, and, at the dawn of the new century, Leo XIII, having proclaimed a jubilee, decided to dedicate the whole human race to the most Sacred Heart. This consecration was actually carried out with solemn rites in all the churches of the Catholic world, and brought about a great increase of this devotion, leading not only nations but even private families to it, who in countless numbers dedicated themselves to the Divine Heart, and submitted themselves to its royal sway. Lastly, the Sovereign Pontiff Pius XI, in order that, by its solemnity, the feast might answer more fully to the greatly widespread devotion of the Christian people, raised the feast of the most Sacred Heart of Jesus to the rite of a double of the first class, with an octave; and moreover, that the violated rights of Christ, the supreme King and most loving Lord, might be repaired, and that the sins of the nations might be bewailed, he ordered that annually, on that same feast-day, there should be recited an expiatory form of prayer in all the churches of the Christian world.

content.latin: Ut de látere Christi dormiéntis in cruce formarétur Ecclésia, et Scriptúra implerétur quæ dicit: Vidébunt in quem transfixérunt, divína est ordinatióne indúltum ut unus mílitum láncea latus illud sacrum aperiéndo perfóderet, quátenus sánguine cum aqua manánte, prétium effunderétur nostræ salútis quod a fonte scílicet Cordis arcáno profúsum, vim daret sacraméntis Ecclésiæ ad vitam grátiæ conferéndam, essétque iam in Christo vivéntibus póculum fontis vivi, saliéntis in vitam ætérnam. Surge ígitur, ánima amíca Christi, vigiláre non cesses, ibi os appóne, ut háurias aquas de fóntibus salvatóris.
content.english: In order that the Church might be taken out of the side of Christ, in his deep sleep on the Cross, and that the Scripture might be fulfilled which saith: They shall look on him whom they pierced: it was divinely ordained that one of the soldiers should pierce his sacred side with a spear, and open it. Then forthwith there came flowing out blood and water, which was the price of our salvation, pouring forth from its mountain-source, in sooth, from the secret places of his Heart, to give power to the Sacraments of the Church, to bestow the life of grace, and to be as a saving drink of living waters, flowing up to life eternal for those who were already quickened in Christ. Arise, then, O soul beloved of Christ. Cease not thy vigilance, place there thy lips, and drink the waters from the fount of salvation.

content.latin: Quia semel vénimus ad Cor Dómini Iesu dulcíssimi, et bonum est nos hic esse, non fácile evellámur ab eo. O quam bonum et iucúndum habitáre in Corde hoc. Bonus thesáurus, pretiósa margaríta Cor tuum, óptime Iesu, quam, fosso agro córporis tui, invenímus. Quis hanc margarítam abíciat? Quin pótius, dabo omnes margarítas, cogitatiónes et affectiónes meas commutábo et comparábo illam mihi, iactans omnem cogitátum meum in Cor boni Iesu, et sine fallácia illud me enútriet. Hoc ígitur tuo et meo Corde, dulcíssime Iesu, invénto, orábo te Deum meum: admítte in sacrárium exauditiónis preces meas: immo me totum trahe in Cor tuum.
content.english: Because we are now come to the sweet Heart of Jesus, and because it is good for us to be here, let us not too soon turn away therefrom. O how good and joyful a thing it is to dwell in this Heart. What a good treasure, what a precious pearl, is thy Heart, O most excellent Jesu, which we have found hidden in the pit which hath been dug in this field, namely, in thy body. Who would cast away such a pearl? Nay, rather, for this same I would give all my pearls. I will sell all my thoughts and affections, and buy the same for myself, turning all my thoughts to the Heart of the good Jesus, and without fail it will support me. Therefore, o most sweet Jesu, finding this Heart that is thine and mine, I will pray to thee, my God: admit my prayers into the shrine of hearkening: and draw me even more altogether into thy Heart.

content.latin: Ad hoc enim perforátum est latus tuum, ut nobis páteat intróitus. Ad hoc vulnerátum est Cor tuum, ut in illo ab exterióribus turbatiónibus absolúti habitáre possímus. Nihilóminus et proptérea vulnerátum est, ut per vulnus visíbile, vulnus amóris invisíbile videámus. Quómodo hic ardor mélius posset osténdi, nisi quod non solum corpus, verum étiam ipsum Cor láncea vulnerári permísit? Carnále ergo vulnus, vulnus spirituále osténdit. Quis illud Cor tam vulnerátum non díligat? quis tam amántem non rédamet? quis tam castum non amplectátur? Nos ígitur adhuc in carne manéntes, quantum póssumus, amántem redamémus, amplectámur vulnerátum nostrum, cuius ímpii agrícolæ fodérunt manus et pedes, latus et Cor; oremúsque ut cor nostrum, adhuc durum et impœ́nitens, amóris sui vínculo constríngere et iáculo vulneráre dignétur.
content.english: For to this end was thy side pierced, that an entry might be open unto us. To this end was thy Heart wounded, that in it we might be able to dwell secure from alarms from without. And it was wounded none the less on this account that, because of the visible wound, we may perceive the wound of love which is invisible. How could this fire of love better shine forth than for him to permit that not only his body, but that even his Heart, should be wounded with the spear? Who would not love that Heart so wounded? Who would not, in return, love one who is so loving? Who would not embrace one so chaste? Wherefore let us who are in the flesh love in return, as much as we can, him who so loveth, embrace our wounded one, whose hands and feet, side and Heart, have been pierced by wicked husbandmen; and let us pray that he may deign to bind our hearts, still hard and impenitent, with the chain of his love, and wound them with the dart thereof.

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.latin: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
content.english: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Fílii tui, nostris vulneráto peccátis, infinítos dilectiónis thesáuros misericórditer largíri dignáris; concéde, quǽsumus, ut illi devótum pietátis nostræ præstántes obséquium, dignæ quoque satisfactiónis exhibeámus offícium.
content.english: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: 118:17 (Ghimel) Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:
content.english: 118:17 (Ghimel) Give bountifully to thy servant, enliven me * and I shall keep thy words.

content.latin: 118:18 Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.
content.english: 118:18 Open thou my eyes: * and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law.

content.latin: 118:19 Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:19 I am a sojourner on the earth: * hide not thy commandments from me.

content.latin: 118:20 Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
content.english: 118:20 My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.

content.latin: 118:21 Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:21 Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:22 Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:23 Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:23 For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:24 Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
content.english: 118:24 For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.

content.latin: 118:25 (Daleth) Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:25 (Daleth) My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:26 Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:26 I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:27 Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
content.english: 118:27 Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.

content.latin: 118:28 Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.
content.english: 118:28 My soul hath slumbered through heaviness: * strengthen thou me in thy words.

content.latin: 118:29 Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.
content.english: 118:29 Remove from me the way of iniquity: * and out of thy law have mercy on me.

content.latin: 118:30 Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.

content.latin: Romæ, via Ardeatína, natális sanctæ Felículæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, nec Flacco núbere neque idólis immoláre volens, trádita est cuídam Iúdici, qui eam in confessióne Christi perseverántem, post tenebricósam custódiam et famis inédiam, támdiu fecit in equúleo torquéri, donec illa emítteret spíritum, et sic demum depóni et in cloácam præcipitári. Ipsíus vero corpus, inde extráctum, sanctus Nicomédes Présbyter eádem via sepelívit.
content.english: At Rome, upon the Ardeatine Way, the holy Virgin martyr Felicula. She would not marry Flaccus nor sacrifice to idols, and was therefore handed over to a certain judge who, forasmuch as she remained steadfast in confessing Christ, starved her in the dark, then had her racked until she died, and thereafter threw her body into a sewer. The holy Nicomedes buried her beside the same Way.

content.latin: In Pelígnis sancti Peregríni, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, pro fide cathólica, a Longobárdis in Atérnum flumen demérsus est.

content.latin: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sancti Fándilæ, Presbýteri et Mónachi; qui, in persecutióne Arábica, amputáto cápite, pro Christi fide martýrium súbiit.
content.english: At Byblos, in Palestine, the holy Virgin martyr Aquilina, aged twelve years. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian and the judge Valusian, she was buffeted and beaten for her confession of the faith, and stabbed with heated awls, and lastly smitten with the sword, and so hallowed maidenhood by martyrdom.

content.latin: 118:33 (He) Legem pone mihi, Dómine, viam iustificatiónum tuárum: * et exquíram eam semper.
content.english: 118:33 (He) Set before me for a law the way of thy justifications, O Lord: * and I will always seek after it.

content.latin: 118:34 Da mihi intelléctum, et scrutábor legem tuam: * et custódiam illam in toto corde meo.
content.english: 118:34 Give me understanding, and I will search thy law; * and I will keep it with my whole heart.

content.latin: 118:35 Deduc me in sémitam mandatórum tuórum: * quia ipsam vólui.
content.english: 118:35 Lead me into the path of thy commandments; * for this same I have desired.

content.latin: 118:36 Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua: * et non in avarítiam.
content.english: 118:36 Incline my heart into thy testimonies * and not to covetousness.

content.latin: 118:37 Avérte óculos meos ne vídeant vanitátem: * in via tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:37 Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity: * quicken me in thy way.

content.latin: 118:38 Státue servo tuo elóquium tuum, * in timóre tuo.
content.english: 118:38 Establish thy word to thy servant, * in thy fear.

content.latin: 118:39 Ámputa oppróbrium meum quod suspicátus sum: * quia iudícia tua iucúnda.
content.english: 118:39 Turn away my reproach, which I have apprehended: * for thy judgments are delightful.

content.latin: 118:40 Ecce, concupívi mandáta tua: * in æquitáte tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:40 Behold I have longed after thy precepts: * quicken me in thy justice.

content.latin: 118:41 (Vav) Et véniat super me misericórdia tua, Dómine: * salutáre tuum secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:41 (Vau) Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord: * thy salvation according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:42 Et respondébo exprobrántibus mihi verbum: * quia sperávi in sermónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:42 So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing; * that I have trusted in thy words.

content.latin: 118:43 Et ne áuferas de ore meo verbum veritátis usquequáque: * quia in iudíciis tuis supersperávi.
content.english: 118:43 And take not thou the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: * for in thy words, I have hoped exceedingly.

content.latin: 118:44 Et custódiam legem tuam semper: * in sǽculum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 118:44 So shall I always keep thy law, * for ever and ever.

content.latin: 118:45 Et ambulábam in latitúdine: * quia mandáta tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:45 And I walked at large: * because I have sought after thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:46 Et loquébar in testimóniis tuis in conspéctu regum: * et non confundébar.
content.english: 118:46 And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: * and I was not ashamed.

content.latin: 118:47 Et meditábar in mandátis tuis, * quæ diléxi.
content.english: 118:47 I meditated also on thy commandments, * which I loved.

content.latin: 118:48 Et levávi manus meas ad mandáta tua, quæ diléxi: * et exercébar in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:48 And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments, which I loved: * and I was exercised in thy justifications.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:49 (Zai) Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo, * in quo mihi spem dedísti.
content.english: 118:49 (Zai) Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant, * in which thou hast given me hope.

content.latin: 118:50 Hæc me consoláta est in humilitáte mea: * quia elóquium tuum vivificávit me.
content.english: 118:50 This hath comforted me in my humiliation: * because thy word hath enlivened me.

content.latin: 118:51 Supérbi iníque agébant usquequáque: * a lege autem tua non declinávi.
content.english: 118:51 The proud did iniquitously altogether: * but I declined not from thy law.

content.latin: 118:52 Memor fui iudiciórum tuórum a sǽculo, Dómine: * et consolátus sum.
content.english: 118:52 I remembered, O Lord, thy judgments of old: * and I was comforted.

content.latin: 118:53 Deféctio ténuit me, * pro peccatóribus derelinquéntibus legem tuam.
content.english: 118:53 A fainting hath taken hold of me, * because of the wicked that forsake thy law.

content.latin: 118:54 Cantábiles mihi erant iustificatiónes tuæ, * in loco peregrinatiónis meæ.
content.english: 118:54 Thy justifications were the subject of my song, * in the place of my pilgrimage.

content.latin: 118:55 Memor fui nocte nóminis tui, Dómine: * et custodívi legem tuam.
content.english: 118:55 In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord: * and have kept thy law.

content.latin: 118:56 Hæc facta est mihi: * quia iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
content.english: 118:56 This happened to me: * because I sought after thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:57 (Heth) Pórtio mea, Dómine, * dixi custodíre legem tuam.
content.english: 118:57 (Heth) O Lord, my portion, * I have said, I would keep thy law.

content.latin: 118:58 Deprecátus sum fáciem tuam in toto corde meo: * miserére mei secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:58 I entreated thy face with all my heart: * have mercy on me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:59 Cogitávi vias meas: * et convérti pedes meos in testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:59 I have thought on my ways: * and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:60 Parátus sum, et non sum turbátus: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:60 I am ready, and am not troubled: * that I may keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:61 Funes peccatórum circumpléxi sunt me: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:61 The cords of the wicked have encompassed me: * but I have not forgotten thy law.

content.latin: 118:62 Média nocte surgébam ad confiténdum tibi, * super iudícia iustificatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 118:62 I rose at midnight to give praise to thee; * for the judgments of thy justification.

content.latin: 118:63 Párticeps ego sum ómnium timéntium te: * et custodiéntium mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:63 I am a partaker with all them that fear thee, * and that keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:64 Misericórdia tua, Dómine, plena est terra: * iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
content.english: 118:64 The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercy: * teach me thy justifications.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: 118:65 (Teth) Bonitátem fecísti cum servo tuo, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:65 (Teth) Thou hast done well with thy servant, O Lord, * according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:66 Bonitátem, et disciplínam, et sciéntiam doce me: * quia mandátis tuis crédidi.
content.english: 118:66 Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge; * for I have believed thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:67 Priúsquam humiliárer ego delíqui: * proptérea elóquium tuum custodívi.
content.english: 118:67 Before I was humbled I offended; * therefore have I kept thy word.

content.latin: 118:68 Bonus es tu: * et in bonitáte tua doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:68 Thou art good; * and in thy goodness teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:69 Multiplicáta est super me iníquitas superbórum: * ego autem in toto corde meo scrutábor mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:69 The iniquity of the proud hath been multiplied over me: * but I will seek thy commandments with my whole heart.

content.latin: 118:70 Coagulátum est sicut lac cor eórum: * ego vero legem tuam meditátus sum.
content.english: 118:70 Their heart is curdled like milk: * but I have meditated on thy law.

content.latin: 118:71 Bonum mihi quia humiliásti me: * ut discam iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:71 It is good for me that thou hast humbled me, * that I may learn thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:72 Bonum mihi lex oris tui, * super míllia auri et argénti.
content.english: 118:72 The law of thy mouth is good to me, * above thousands of gold and silver.

content.latin: 118:73 (Ioth) Manus tuæ fecérunt me, et plasmavérunt me: * da mihi intelléctum, et discam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:73 (Jod) Thy hands have made me and formed me: * give me understanding, and I will learn thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:74 Qui timent te vidébunt me, et lætabúntur: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
content.english: 118:74 They that fear thee shall see me, and shall be glad: * because I have greatly hoped in thy words.

content.latin: 118:75 Cognóvi, Dómine, quia ǽquitas iudícia tua: * et in veritáte tua humiliásti me.
content.english: 118:75 I know, O Lord, that thy judgments are equity: * and in thy truth thou hast humbled me.

content.latin: 118:76 Fiat misericórdia tua ut consolétur me, * secúndum elóquium tuum servo tuo.
content.english: 118:76 O! let thy mercy be for my comfort, * according to thy word unto thy servant.

content.latin: 118:77 Véniant mihi miseratiónes tuæ, et vivam: * quia lex tua meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:77 Let thy tender mercies come unto me, and I shall live: * for thy law is my meditation.

content.latin: 118:78 Confundántur supérbi, quia iniúste iniquitátem fecérunt in me: * ego autem exercébor in mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:78 Let the proud be ashamed, because they have done unjustly towards me: * but I will be employed in thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:79 Convertántur mihi timéntes te: * et qui novérunt testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:79 Let them that fear thee turn to me: * and they that know thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:80 Fiat cor meum immaculátum in iustificatiónibus tuis, * ut non confúndar.
content.english: 118:80 Let my heart be undefiled in thy justifications, * that I may not be confounded.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Stans Iesus clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
content.english: Ant. Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

content.latin: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
content.english: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟.br. Tóllite iugum meum super vos * Et díscite a me.
content.english: ℟.br. Take my yoke upon you * And learn of me.

content.latin: ℟. Tóllite iugum meum super vos * Et díscite a me.
content.english: ℟. Take my yoke upon you * And learn of me.

content.latin: ℣. Quia mitis sum et húmilis Corde.
content.english: ℣. For I am meek and lowly in Heart.

content.latin: ℟. Et díscite a me.
content.english: ℟. And learn of me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Tóllite iugum meum super vos * Et díscite a me.
content.english: ℟. Take my yoke upon you * And learn of me.

content.latin: ℣. Ego dixi, Dómine, miserére mei.
content.english: ℣. I said: Lord, be merciful unto me.

content.latin: ℟. Sana ánimam meam quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: ℟. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Fílii tui, nostris vulneráto peccátis, infinítos dilectiónis thesáuros misericórditer largíri dignáris; concéde, quǽsumus, ut illi devótum pietátis nostræ præstántes obséquium, dignæ quoque satisfactiónis exhibeámus offícium.
content.english: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
content.english: Ant. With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

content.latin: 118:81 (Caph) Defécit in salutáre tuum ánima mea: * et in verbum tuum supersperávi.
content.english: 118:81 (Caph) My soul hath fainted after thy salvation: * and in thy word I have very much hoped.

content.latin: 118:82 Defecérunt óculi mei in elóquium tuum, * dicéntes: Quando consoláberis me?
content.english: 118:82 My eyes have failed for thy word, * saying: When wilt thou comfort me?

content.latin: 118:83 Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruína: * iustificatiónes tuas non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:83 For I am become like a bottle in the frost: * I have not forgotten thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:84 Quot sunt dies servi tui? * quando fácies de persequéntibus me iudícium?
content.english: 118:84 How many are the days of thy servant: * when wilt thou execute judgment on them that persecute me?

content.latin: 118:85 Narravérunt mihi iníqui fabulatiónes: * sed non ut lex tua.
content.english: 118:85 The wicked have told me fables: * but not as thy law.

content.latin: 118:86 Ómnia mandáta tua véritas: * iníque persecúti sunt me, ádiuva me.
content.english: 118:86 All thy statutes are truth: * they have persecuted me unjustly, do thou help me.

content.latin: 118:87 Paulo minus consummavérunt me in terra: * ego autem non derelíqui mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:87 They had almost made an end of me upon earth: * but I have not forsaken thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:88 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam vivífica me: * et custódiam testimónia oris tui.
content.english: 118:88 Quicken thou me according to thy mercy: * and I shall keep the testimonies of thy mouth.

content.latin: 118:89 (Lamed) In ætérnum, Dómine, * verbum tuum pérmanet in cælo.
content.english: 118:89 (Lamed) For ever, O Lord, * thy word standeth firm in heaven.

content.latin: 118:90 In generatiónem et generatiónem véritas tua: * fundásti terram, et pérmanet.
content.english: 118:90 Thy truth unto all generations: * thou hast founded the earth, and it continueth.

content.latin: 118:91 Ordinatióne tua persevérat dies: * quóniam ómnia sérviunt tibi.
content.english: 118:91 By thy ordinance the day goeth on: * for all things serve thee.

content.latin: 118:92 Nisi quod lex tua meditátio mea est: * tunc forte periíssem in humilitáte mea.
content.english: 118:92 Unless thy law had been my meditation, * I had then perhaps perished in my abjection.

content.latin: 118:93 In ætérnum non oblivíscar iustificatiónes tuas: * quia in ipsis vivificásti me.
content.english: 118:93 Thy justifications I will never forget: * for by them thou hast given me life.

content.latin: 118:94 Tuus sum ego, salvum me fac: * quóniam iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
content.english: 118:94 I am thine, save thou me: * for I have sought thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:95 Me exspectavérunt peccatóres ut pérderent me: * testimónia tua intelléxi.
content.english: 118:95 The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: * but I have understood thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:96 Omnis consummatiónis vidi finem: * latum mandátum tuum nimis.
content.english: 118:96 I have seen an end of all perfection: * thy commandment is exceeding broad.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:97 (Mem) Quómodo diléxi legem tuam, Dómine? * tota die meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:97 (Mem) How have I loved thy law, O Lord! * it is my meditation all the day.

content.latin: 118:98 Super inimícos meos prudéntem me fecísti mandáto tuo: * quia in ætérnum mihi est.
content.english: 118:98 Through thy commandment, thou hast made me wiser than my enemies: * for it is ever with me.

content.latin: 118:99 Super omnes docéntes me intelléxi: * quia testimónia tua meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:99 I have understood more than all my teachers: * because thy testimonies are my meditation.

content.latin: 118:100 Super senes intelléxi: * quia mandáta tua quæsívi.
content.english: 118:100 I have had understanding above ancients: * because I have sought thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:101 Ab omni via mala prohíbui pedes meos: * ut custódiam verba tua.
content.english: 118:101 I have restrained my feet from every evil way: * that I may keep thy words.

content.latin: 118:102 A iudíciis tuis non declinávi: * quia tu legem posuísti mihi.
content.english: 118:102 I have not declined from thy judgments, * because thou hast set me a law.

content.latin: 118:103 Quam dúlcia fáucibus meis elóquia tua, * super mel ori meo!
content.english: 118:103 How sweet are thy words to my palate! * more than honey to my mouth.

content.latin: 118:104 A mandátis tuis intelléxi: * proptérea odívi omnem viam iniquitátis.
content.english: 118:104 By thy commandments I have had understanding: * therefore have I hated every way of iniquity.

content.latin: 118:105 (Nun) Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, * et lumen sémitis meis.
content.english: 118:105 (Nun) Thy word is a lamp to my feet, * and a light to my paths.

content.latin: 118:106 Iurávi, et státui * custodíre iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:106 I have sworn and am determined * to keep the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:107 Humiliátus sum usquequáque, Dómine: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:107 I have been humbled, O Lord, exceedingly: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:108 Voluntária oris mei beneplácita fac, Dómine: * et iudícia tua doce me.
content.english: 118:108 The free offerings of my mouth make acceptable, O Lord: * and teach me thy judgments.

content.latin: 118:109 Ánima mea in mánibus meis semper: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:109 My soul is continually in my hands: * and I have not forgotten thy law.

content.latin: 118:110 Posuérunt peccatóres láqueum mihi: * et de mandátis tuis non errávi.
content.english: 118:110 Sinners have laid a snare for me: * but I have not erred from thy precepts.

content.latin: 118:111 Hereditáte acquisívi testimónia tua in ætérnum: * quia exsultátio cordis mei sunt.
content.english: 118:111 I have purchased thy testimonies for an inheritance for ever: * because they are the joy of my heart.

content.latin: 118:112 Inclinávi cor meum ad faciéndas iustificatiónes tuas in ætérnum, * propter retributiónem.
content.english: 118:112 I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications for ever, * for the reward.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:113 (Samech) Iníquos ódio hábui: * et legem tuam diléxi.
content.english: 118:113 (Samech) I have hated the unjust: * and I have loved thy law.

content.latin: 118:114 Adiútor et suscéptor meus es tu: * et in verbum tuum supersperávi.
content.english: 118:114 Thou art my helper and my protector: * and in thy word I have greatly hoped.

content.latin: 118:115 Declináte a me, malígni: * et scrutábor mandáta Dei mei.
content.english: 118:115 Depart from me, ye malignant: * and I will search the commandments of my God.

content.latin: 118:116 Súscipe me secúndum elóquium tuum, et vivam: * et non confúndas me ab exspectatióne mea.
content.english: 118:116 Uphold me according to thy word, and I shall live: * and let me not be confounded in my expectation.

content.latin: 118:117 Ádiuva me, et salvus ero: * et meditábor in iustificatiónibus tuis semper.
content.english: 118:117 Help me, and I shall be saved: * and I will meditate always on thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:118 Sprevísti omnes discedéntes a iudíciis tuis: * quia iniústa cogitátio eórum.
content.english: 118:118 Thou hast despised all them that fall off from thy judgments; * for their thought is unjust.

content.latin: 118:119 Prævaricántes reputávi omnes peccatóres terræ: * ídeo diléxi testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:119 I have accounted all the sinners of the earth prevaricators: * therefore have I loved thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:120 Confíge timóre tuo carnes meas: * a iudíciis enim tuis tímui.
content.english: 118:120 Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear: * for I am afraid of thy judgments.

content.latin: 118:121 (Ain) Feci iudícium et iustítiam: * non tradas me calumniántibus me.
content.english: 118:121 (Ain) I have done judgment and justice: * give me not up to them that slander me.

content.latin: 118:122 Súscipe servum tuum in bonum: * non calumniéntur me supérbi.
content.english: 118:122 Uphold thy servant unto good: * let not the proud calumniate me.

content.latin: 118:123 Óculi mei defecérunt in salutáre tuum: * et in elóquium iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:123 My eyes have fainted after thy salvation: * and for the word of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:124 Fac cum servo tuo secúndum misericórdiam tuam: * et iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
content.english: 118:124 Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy: * and teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:125 Servus tuus sum ego: * da mihi intelléctum, ut sciam testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:125 I am thy servant: * give me understanding that I may know thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:126 Tempus faciéndi, Dómine: * dissipavérunt legem tuam.
content.english: 118:126 It is time, O Lord, to do: * they have dissipated thy law.

content.latin: 118:127 Ídeo diléxi mandáta tua, * super aurum et topázion.
content.english: 118:127 Therefore have I loved thy commandments * above gold and the topaz.

content.latin: 118:128 Proptérea ad ómnia mandáta tua dirigébar: * omnem viam iníquam ódio hábui.
content.english: 118:128 Therefore was I directed to all thy commandments: * I have hated all wicked ways.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In caritáte perpétua diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
content.english: Ant. With an everlasting love hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

content.latin: Huius rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ virtúte corroborári per Spíritum eius in interiórem hóminem: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.
content.english: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟.br. Ego dixi: Dómine, * Miserére mei.
content.english: ℟.br. I said: Lord, * Be merciful unto me.

content.latin: ℟. Ego dixi: Dómine, * Miserére mei.
content.english: ℟. I said: Lord, * Be merciful unto me.

content.latin: ℣. Sana ánimam meam quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: ℣. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

content.latin: ℟. Miserére mei.
content.english: ℟. Be merciful unto me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Ego dixi: Dómine, * Miserére mei.
content.english: ℟. I said: Lord, * Be merciful unto me.

content.latin: ℣. Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum miserátor Dóminus.
content.english: ℣. The merciful Lord hath instituted a memorial of his wondrous deeds.

content.latin: ℟. Escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: ℟. He hath given meat unto them that fear him.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: Let us pray.

content.english: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.
